title: October 29 — phase state, feedback relay, and a residue-trained returning loop
summary: Seven new source-reviewed repositories. Complexity isolates a persistent internal field change; two chain studies separate beat codes, threshold slips and limited state transfer; ThursdaySol finds a fragile history-graft response. MoebiusLoopMemory and LoopAImemory show synthetic trained temporal readouts without a special Möbius advantage. Newly implemented RoundAndRound reawakens a completely erased fast loop using a learned Sihti-residue map; direct-state ridge ties exactly, ruling out a claimed compression advantage.

nodes.claim: A continuously evolving fast phase state leaves Sihti-style ringdown residues; slow cue-to-residue ridge is trained and restores state after complete fast erasure.
nodes.survived: Five local tests passed. A 12-history, 8-repeat first gate shows cue-trained reawakening RMSE 0.22174 after fast reset, wrong cue 3.67203, empty state 2.95856; telescoping identity error 3.55e-15.
nodes.killed: Direct cue-to-state ridge ties at RMSE 0.22174, as required for linear telescoping. No demonstrated compression, unsupervised consolidation, long-term continual learning or neural mechanism.
nodes.era: October 29: circulating state and residue reawakening

nodes.claim: Reuses the fixed recurrent state of MoebiusLoopMemory with a trained linear readout and a dual-path synthetic temporal classifier/predictor.
nodes.survived: Source reports 99.9% held-out dual-path event equality, 100% lag-6 recall and 91.1% second-order synthetic future prediction.
nodes.killed: A quadratic mean baseline scores 100% on equality, a two-frame oracle ties prediction, and a signed gated loop fails a delayed/noisier OOD test. Real webcam generalization is unmeasured.
nodes.era: October 29: circulating state and residue reawakening

nodes.claim: Fixed rotating feature-state with apical-inspired multiplicative contextual gating and a strictly linear output head.
nodes.survived: Five-seed signed+gate historical XOR(lags 2,3) 83.3% and lag-6 recall 75.9%; history-erasure control falls to chance. Ungated shift recalls individual past bits better.
nodes.killed: Ordinary cyclic and random orthogonal loops tie or beat the signed shift on these tested tasks. No special Möbius benefit, physical traveling wave or brain claim.
nodes.era: October 29: circulating state and residue reawakening

nodes.claim: Three deliberately coupled homeostatic/checkerboard feedback loops reconstruct and extend the Perception Lab ECG graph.
nodes.survived: A deterministic matched-state history graft at B changes downstream C's later probe interaction by 0.666833; cutting B→C yields zero.
nodes.killed: Default noisy robustness gate fails: 0/8 paired preparations above 0.05 at input noise SD 0.003. Couplings and graft are engineered, not biological relay.
nodes.era: October 29: circulating state and residue reawakening

nodes.claim: Independent analysis of phase-coded two-tone beating, propagation and engineered stationary receiving oscillators.
nodes.survived: Source reports measured near-field contrast decay and stationary active receiver state re-emission/history-dependent response.
nodes.killed: Prescribed passive tones do not constitute neuronal threshold spikes; moving bonded-chain regeneration and robust long-range relay have not been shown.
nodes.era: October 29: circulating state and residue reawakening

nodes.claim: Tests pumped phase-coded chain beats, near-critical 2π phase slips and transfer to neighbors using original oscillator field dynamics.
nodes.survived: A d=3 receiver classifies sender patterns 0.85 versus leakage control 0.62; a near-complement pair exhibits threshold-like slips near a locking edge.
nodes.killed: Original chain bursts are ordinary beats; reliable regenerative multi-hop spike relay remains unproved.
nodes.era: October 29: circulating state and residue reawakening

nodes.claim: Simulated seeded field droplets are tested for geometric recovery, lingering changed response and compact local prediction.
nodes.survived: Source reports changed breathing state with recovery in 11/11 seeded droplets; local held-out probe prediction error falls from 0.402 to 0.218 with internal phase variables.
nodes.killed: Objects are seeded and finite-lived; full-world dynamics and generic morphology need not generate useful persistent objects. No general consciousness or memory law follows.
nodes.era: October 29: circulating state and residue reawakening

edges.why: LoopAImemory explicitly reuses the recurrence from MoebiusLoopMemory with trained task readouts.
RoundAndRound carries the circulating-state research question forward with continuous-time rotation and Sihti trained residues, rather than copying the shift implementation.
Both ask whether a learned reader can use bounded history; RoundAndRound adds fast-state erasure and a separately trained association to restore the state.
Sol independently audits beat physics and receiver state alongside Claude's chain experiment, rather than reproducing a claimed biological spike.

motifs.title: Fast circulation, slow association and reactivation are separate mechanisms
motifs.description: MoebiusLoopMemory and LoopAImemory make temporal history accessible to trained readouts. RoundAndRound trains a cue-to-ringdown-residue memory, erases all fast activity and reactivates it. A direct ridge tie is the central negative control: the decomposition alone yields no extra information.

motifs.title: Retained changes are not automatically regenerated or transmitted spikes
motifs.description: Complexity's seeded droplet, ThursdaySol's controller history, and independent Claude/Sol chain experiments show different forms of history-dependent response. Their noise, distance, fixed-geometry and intervention limits remain distinct.
